judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard claims-made legend whose operative content ('first made ... and reported in writing ... pursuant to the terms herein') simply cross-refers to the body of the policy; no term in it is genuinely two-sided on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Insuring Agreement I and Section V.A, though it omits the 60-day post-expiration tail and the ERP deeming rule in II.C, leaving only a small gap between the legend and the operative reporting terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The condition that the Policy 'shall not be valid unless also signed by another duly authorized representative' is oddly circular (officers already signed) and could be read to make validity turn on a countersignature that may or may not appear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy addresses countersignature; Section VIII.K on endorsements signed by an authorized representative is consistent rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short consideration/reliance recital; 'in reliance on all Statements made in the Application' is broad but is defined and elaborated elsewhere rather than ambiguous here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a recital of reliance sitting against operative Section VIII.B (severability of the Application) and VIII.K's entire-agreement sentence, a classic recital-vs-operative tension over what the Application does to coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant is garbled — 'made against any Insured by or on behalf Employee' drops words — and it couples an open-ended 'as soon as practicable' duty with a hard sixty-day outside date, a pairing insureds and insurers routinely read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with Section V.A (Claims deemed first made on the earlier date under any prior policy), II.C (ERP claims deemed made in the preceding Policy Period) and VI.A/VI.C's separate notice clocks, which do not line up cleanly with the sixty-day tail stated here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The extension is carefully bounded and its own last sentence defines 'spouse'; the only wrinkle is capitalised 'Spouse' being used as if defined when it is not.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Section III.I/III.J (Insured, Insured Individual) and Section III.L (Loss) without visible tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain derivative-coverage language with an express carve-out for the representatives' own wrongful acts; nothing on the face invites two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the definitions of Insured Individual and Loss and with Section VIII.I (Bankruptcy); no competing provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger is one-sided and incomplete — the ERP arises only if the Insurer non-renews or the Parent Company cancels, saying nothing about Parent Company non-renewal — and 'given by the insured' leaves who may elect uncertain as between Policyholder and Insured Individuals.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with VIII.C (cancellation/non-renewal notice), Item 5 of the Declarations and VIII.J (which excepts ERP notice from the Parent Company's authority), and its deeming of ERP claims into the preceding Policy Period sits awkwardly against Insuring Agreement I's separate ERP language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'each and every signed application ... other materials submitted therewith ... and any other such documents submitted in connection with the underwriting' is an open catch-all after enumerated specifics, and its reach into public DOL/EEOC filings is genuinely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds Section VIII.B (representations and severability) and the preamble's reliance language, so its breadth directly affects a rescission/misrepresentation dispute, but no direct contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any other payment to or for the benefit of an employee arising out of the employment relationship' is a broad catch-all trailing a specific list, though the final sentence carves out salary and commissions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Benefits are also excluded from Loss (III.L.4 and L.6) and made defence-costs-only by Exclusion B.1, an overlap that requires harmonising but is not plainly contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One line; 'implied employment contract' is broad but is a familiar legal category rather than a two-meaning term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expands coverage while Exclusion A.4 and Exclusion B.3 pull contractual liability back out, so the interaction between grant and exclusions is a live harmonising question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is the coverage trigger and its components — 'a written demand ... for monetary or non-monetary relief', 'similar formal proceeding', 'commenced by a notice of charges ... or similar document' — are exactly the phrases parties fight over in deciding what and when a Claim is; the collective-bargaining carve-out adds a further scope question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be read with III.R (Potential Claim), VI.A's awareness provision and V.A's rule deeming related Claims first made on the earliest date under this or any prior policy, all of which bear on whether a demand became a Claim in this policy year.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonable and necessary legal fees and expenses' is a standard but inherently contestable measure, though the parenthetical exclusions are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with V.A (defence costs erode limits), V.C (consent) and Exclusion B (defence-costs-only); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very broad ('any Federal, State, or local statute, regulation, ordinance or common law concerning discrimination in employment anywhere in the world') but breadth here favours the insured and is not two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds Wrongful Employment Act (III.X) and is cut back by Exclusion A.5's law-based exclusions, an overlap that mostly works.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Item 5 ('any individual contracted to perform work ... but only if such individual performs work or services solely for or on behalf of the Policyholder') and the 'solely directed' qualifier in item 3 create real line-drawing problems.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Employee overlaps heavily with Insured Individual (III.J) and cuts against III.V and Exclusion A.9, which push independent contractors out of coverage — so a contractor may be an Employee claimant yet excluded elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subparagraph 3, 'illegal work related harassment', is a bare catch-all appended to two specific sexual-harassment definitions, the classic general-vs-specific problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds III.X and is limited by exclusions rather than contradicted by them; no conflicting provision identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line definition with two defined components; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently throughout; the only friction is that Insuring Agreement A contemplates Claims by an Employee against an Insured where the two categories overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Categories are conditioned on written indemnity agreements and on direction of labour, which are workable tests, though the overlap of items 2 and 3 with 'Employee' invites argument about which hat a claimant wears.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because III.G (Employee) covers much the same people, a person may be both claimant and Insured under Insuring Agreement A, a whole-instrument wrinkle the policy never resolves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'common nexus [of] any fact, circumstance, situation, event, transaction, cause or series of causally or logically connected' facts is famously elastic — 'logically connected' has no discernible boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives V.A's single-Claim/relation-back rule and Exclusion A.2(b)'s prior-claim bar, so its reach determines whether a Claim belongs to this policy year at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long definition with nine carve-outs, several of which are contestable ('matters uninsurable under the law applicable to this Policy', amounts the Insureds are 'legally or financially absolved from payment'), and the most-favourable-jurisdiction punitive rule adds choice-of-law complexity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps Exclusion B.1 and B.3 (Benefits and contract amounts) and Item 6 of the Declarations on punitive damages; the overlaps require harmonising but I found no square contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list is mis-numbered (two items numbered 5, one numbered 3) and 'failure to grant or adopt adequate employment related policies and procedures' is vague; the trailing 'but only when alleged as part of a Claim for' limiter also raises scope questions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its limiter ties it to Breach of Employment Contract, Discrimination, Harassment, Retaliation and Wrongful Job Action, and Exclusion A.8 removes emotional distress in part, an interaction that needs reconciling with item 5's emotional-distress tort.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure pointer to Item 1 of the Declarations; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 1 names FINRA and every downstream use is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward aggregation of Parent Company and Subsidiaries with a bankruptcy gloss; no contested term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on III.U (Subsidiary) and VIII.A, whose timing rules are themselves murky, but Policyholder itself does not conflict with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition contains a bad cross-reference: it points to 'Section VII.C' but Section VII is Notices and cancellation is Section VIII.C, a mechanical error going to when the Policy Period ends.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mis-citation is only resolvable by reading VIII.C (Cancellation/Nonrenewal), and Policy Period drives the trigger in Insuring Agreement I, II.C and V.A, so the error ripples through the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Extremely broad ('any substance ... exhibiting any hazardous characteristics', 'noise', 'odor'), which is expansive drafting for the insurer's benefit but rarely two-sided in an employment policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in Exclusion A.7, which carves back Retaliation claims; the fit is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'an allegation or accusation ... provided such allegation does not constitute a Claim, but subsequently may give rise to a Claim' is circular and its boundary against a 'written demand' Claim is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the hinge of Section VI's awareness provision and sits directly against III.D's definition of Claim; whether a matter was a Potential Claim or already a Claim decides which policy year responds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite and specific — it names ADEA, EPA and FMLA liquidated damages; nothing vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with III.L.9 and Item 6 of the Declarations (Punitive Damages Coverage: Yes), which restores punitive damages 'to the extent insurable'; the interaction is complex but coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the illegal retaliatory treatment of Employees, including any retaliatory treatment against an Employee for' four listed activities — 'including' leaves it unclear whether the list is exhaustive or illustrative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Retaliation is the express carve-back from Exclusions A.5 and A.7, so its scope determines how much of those exclusions survives — a real whole-instrument pressure point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing timing clause is syntactically tangled ('on or before the effective date ... or after the effective date ... if the entity is covered pursuant to Section VIII.A.1, solely with regard to Wrongful Acts occurring at or after'), leaving the temporal condition hard to parse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to VIII.A.1, whose 10%/110% employee thresholds leave acquisitions in between unaddressed, so the two provisions do not mesh cleanly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'who is, or attempted to be, a customer or vendor' is loose, but the definition is otherwise closed and the contractor exclusion is explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It excludes independent contractors while III.G and III.J bring contractors inside 'Employee'/'Insured Individual', and Exclusion A.9 adds a further contractor bar — a coordination question across three provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-branch definition composed entirely of other defined terms; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Insuring Agreement I, III.X and III.Z; no conflict.
